Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA Quezon Avenue. West Triangle, Quezon City http: ltww•w. dilg.gov.ph 22 DILG OPINION NO. NITY. KRISTINE GRACE L SUAREZ Office of the Provincial Legal Officer City Of Calapan, Oriental Mindoro Dear Atty. Suarez: This has reference to your letter dated 24 July 2018 requesting for enlightenment on what particular law and applicable provisions should govern in case of alteration or change of boundaries between two municipalities covered by two different provinces relative to the boundary dispute confronting the provinces of Oriental and Occidental Mindoro. In settling boundary disputes between Local Government Units, Section 118 of R.A. No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 ", provides: "Sec. 118. Jurisdictional Responsibility for Settlement of Boundary Dispute. Boundary disputes between and among local government units shall, as much as possible, be settled amicably. To this end: (a) Boundary disputes involving two (2) or more barangays in the same city or municipality shall be referred for settlement to the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned. (b) Boundary disputes involving two (2) or more municipalities within the same province shall be referred for settlement to the sangguniang panlalawigan concerned. (c) Boundary disputes involving municipalities or component cities of different provinces shall be jointly referred for settlement to the sanggunians of the provinces concerned. (d) Boundary disputes involving a component city or municipality on the one hand and a highly urbanized city on the other, or two (2) or more highly urbanized cities, shall be jointly r€ferred for settlement to the respective sanggunians of the parties. (e) In the event the sanggunian./åils to effect an amicable settlement within sixty (60) days from the date the dispute was referred thereto, it shall issue a certification to that effect. Theregfter, the dispute shall be formally tried by the

sanggunian concerned which shall decide the issue within sixty (60) days from the date of the certification referred to above. ' Hence, following the above-quoted provision of the law, in the settlement of boundary disputes involving two (2) or more municipalities of different provinces, it is the provision under paragraph (c), Section 118 of the Local Government Code that governs. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY L C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary for Local Governme t
